explanation: The declaration is the conference's own act, and the article says so: on 26 July 1945 Truman, Churchill and Chiang Kai-shek "issued the document, which outlined the terms of surrender for the Empire of Japan, **as agreed upon at the Potsdam Conference**". § Drafting shows the conference doing the work — the American delegation opened with a proclamation demanding unconditional surrender, "the Potsdam Declaration went through many drafts until a version acceptable to all was found", and Stalin declined to endorse it there because the Soviet Union was not yet at war with Japan.
